items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (buildWindowsSql, validateWindowName, WindowSpec, WindowDefinition), the code was run through dprint, and the helpers carry JSDoc. One small inconsistency: pg/gel import buildWindowsSql from '~/sql/index.ts' while mysql, sqlite and singlestore import it from functions/window.ts.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: SQL building is shared well through one buildWindowsSql per dialect. But the agent added an unrequested callback form, `typeof spec === 'function' ? spec(new Proxy(this.config.fields, new SelectionProxyHandler(...)))`, and copy-pasted it into all five select builders.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are checked at the boundaries: validateWindowName rejects empty and whitespace-only names, and the ntile/nthValue/frame checks are covered by tests. Positional numbers are not turned into bound params (tests assert params toEqual([])). Hidden tests passed 130/130.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: The change is purely additive. Each of the five *SelectConfig types gets an optional `windows?: WindowDefinition[]`, and pg, mysql, sqlite, singlestore and gel all get the same .window(). windowsSql is undefined when no window is defined, so existing SQL is unchanged. The new helpers are exported through functions/index.ts.
